title: Unique atomless stationary Berkovich probability measures for finitely generated non-elementary random matrix groups over the complex Laurent-series field
author: Romain Dujardin; Charles Favre
work: Degenerations of SL(2, C) representations and Lyapunov exponents
source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue 2 (2019), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/ahl.24
difficulty_reason: The author obtains boundary stationarity without local compactness by combining Berkovich compactification, hyperbolic contractions, a martingale limit argument and concentration on classical points. This non-Archimedean extension of random matrix theory exceeds ordinary qualifying probability and geometry.

primary_locator.selected_hypotheses: k=C((t)) with t-adic norm, countable support generating finitely generated non-elementary group; no moment assumption
primary_locator.required_core: complete author projective/tree and compact-limit-set construction, stationary martingale contraction, uniformly small balls, atomlessness and full classical-point concentration

source_scope_note: The selected problem is the stationary-measure part of Theorem 3.1 over the complex Laurent-series field with its t-adic norm, for countable support generating a finitely generated non-elementary group in the exact proximal/strongly-irreducible sense of Definition 2.17. No moment assumption is imposed for this selected conclusion. The complete author body retains all local projective/tree, compact-limit-set, martingale/Dirac-contraction, uniformly-small-ball, atomlessness and classical-point concentration arguments, including the deferred Lemma 3.8 proof. The Lyapunov, Furstenberg-formula, degeneration and hybrid-space conclusions are unselected context; named Berkovich/probability foundations remain references.
